items.text: Once again, thank you for playing Military Logistics Simulator and thank you for all the comments and feedback you've been sending us for the past week. We have now released an update that aims to answer the issues you mentioned the most.

We have introduced the forklift into the game. You can drive it, and manipulate the mast and tines. Objectives in most missions have been modified, so that completing them will require you to use the forklift.
These tasks are a little more challenging than before, but there are systems that will help you navigate the new mechanics:
when you play in the first person perspective, you will notice a small tablet in the cabin that helps you see the position of tines and the cargo
cargo will also snap to shelves when you put it away with a forklift

if you drop cargo and it falls sideways, you can try to push it back in the right position like a pro, or you can just wait 25s for it to reset: Please note, you will still have objectives where you carry things by hand, or put them in your inventory, but you will no longer carry the largest containers, big pallets, etc. by hand. Only when you assemble turrets, some very heavy objects will be handled the old way.

We have improved the way the game saves your progress. In single player, every time you complete a mission and report to an NPC, the game saves. If you leave the game and return later, you will begin at that "checkpoint", until you reach the end of another phase, or the end of the whole mission.

In multiplayer, save is not implemented. This is because every time you play the multiplayer session, all missions are simply available. You can play them in any order you like. You can open FOSCON (the in-game console for truck, convoy and task management) and select any of the avaialble missions. You can also talk to NPCs and just ask them for jobs, in any order you like.
When you begin multiplayer session, the marker will indicate Quartermaster Anderson, but the dialogue will no longer force you to take his mission.
We have updated how the AI drives in the game, but since some undesired behaviour may still occur, please note:
some missions have been modified, so that they don't rely so heavily on AI vehicles' pathfinding, but rather on convoys led by the player

in case a vehicle is stuck, you can recover it and change its target with FOSCON; you can still also recover player-controlled vehicles and yourself: Other minor changes and bug fixes are part of the update, too, of course.: We'll appreciate your feedback. Let us know what you think when you give the update a try, and if you enjoy it, we'll be greateful for good reviews.: Thank you! Merry Christmas!
Attention!

Thank you for playing Military Logistics Simulator during Next Fest. The festival is over, but we have decided to leave the demo running for a little while longer. We have also uploaded one more update to include some of your feedback.

Among a bunch of smaller fixes, the changes include modified mission dialogue and new encubrance mechanics. Also, settings menus will scale better to different types of monitors. Have fun with the demo, wishlist the game to receive news and updates, and let us know what you think about the changes.
Stay vigilant!
Nano Games Team
Soldiers!

Thank you for playing the Military Logistics Simulator demo and sending us your opinions. We've updated the demo to include as much of your feedback as possible during Next Fest. What are the changes about?

There's more focus put on the missions you seem to like the most - the ones regarding the defense of the base. And there's a little more combat, too. Also, we've been working on performance. And some bugs have been squashed.
We hope you'll enjoy the changes.
Stay vigilant!
Nano Games Team
